candidate.title: sciHi-C
candidate.scope: The central Illumina row, labeled Single-cell combinatorial indexed Hi-C (sciHi-C), at schematic scope, with its implementation association resolved to Ramani et al., Massively multiplex single-cell Hi-C (2017; PMID 28135255; DOI 10.1038/nmeth.4155). The target is chromatin contact organization within individual nuclei; sequenced carriers are barcoded genomic DNA ligation products. The independent scTHS-seq and Dip-C rows are neighboring catalogue entries, not alternatives or branches of this assigned sciHi-C card. The two magnified ligation panels explain operations on the central route. Three representative wells per indexing round are retained as separate local ligations; these icons do not specify the total plate size. Fixed cells are the depicted prepared input. Paper-supported lysis within second-round wells clarifies the compartment-to-DNA interface inside the second barcode block; routine unshown library preparation and analysis settings are outside this extraction.

states.label: Paired-end reads of indexed chromatin ligation products
features: The sequenced carrier is genomic DNA ligation-product library, not chromatin proteins or RNA.
Reads identify genome-derived fragments together with internal bridge-adaptor and external Y-adaptor barcodes.

The barcode combination is the cellular index. Grouping contact observations by this index supports single-cell contact probability maps; computational decomposition is a paper-supported readout interpretation, not a separately depicted preparation operation.

Combinatorial assignment is probabilistic: most barcode combinations identify one nucleus, but collisions can combine multiple nuclei. The paper notes that species-mixture validation cannot detect within-species collisions.
Readout concerns relative chromatin contact probabilities; the schematic does not promise exhaustive recovery of contacts or a direct complete three-dimensional structure.
